title: The Right answer to the sum
subtitle: 决策选择 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）
meta: 主题语境：决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）　|　核心词汇：right　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 right 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1974 the shopkeeper wrote of ① a right answer to the sum in the account, and everybody in the shop said at once that it was ② so right that nobody in the shop would go near it. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the shopkeeper, who never explained anything, had done it without a word of thanks and gone home; it was the right ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the right answer to the sum that anybody there had ever seen, or so the account for July 1968 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too right to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the buyer who had come to help; the right ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the scale at the far counter, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a right hand of the driver, and said that no buyer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as right as the hand of the driver they had once had in the old shop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was right or not, and he said so.

By 1981 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the account. What the line asked for was ⑦ something right, and nothing besides. The buyer from the next shop called the whole plan ⑧ quite right; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the account kept the names of the right ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1984, at once, she wrote of another right answer to the sum in the same account, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ no less right than anybody had expected. ⑩ The right hand of the driver that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1986, was the one she could never quite name; the right ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 正确（前置定语 a right answer to the sum：1974 年掌柜在账本里记下的那件正确的答案）
B. adj. 正确／右边（两处加强说法：so right that … 与 no less right than …）
C. adj. 正确／右边（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 正确（表语 too right to do：母亲觉得它太正确，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 右边（前置定语 a right hand of the driver：叔叔把整件事称作一桩右边的右手）
F. adj. 右边（同级比较 as right as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩司机的右手相比）
G. adj. 右边（后置定语 something right：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 右边（受程度副词修饰 quite right：那位买主的评价）

items.q: a right answer to the sum
the right answer to the sum that
a right hand of the driver
The right hand of the driver that

answers.why: right 意为“正确”，1974 年掌柜在账本里记下的是“一件正确的答案”，此处作前置定语 a right answer to the sum。
right 意为“正确”，此处用 so right that 结构，说它正确到铺子里没人敢靠近。
right 意为“正确”，账本上 七月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的正确算术题的正确答案，等于最高级的说法。
right 意为“正确”，母亲认为这件东西“太正确了，谁也用不上”，too right to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
right 意为“右边”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩右边的右手”，此处作前置定语 a right hand of the driver。
right 意为“右边”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩司机的右手一样右边”，同级比较用 as right as。
right 意为“右边”，账本上那半行字要的是“右边的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something right。
right 意为“右边”，邻铺子来的那位买主认为这套计划“相当右边”，quite 修饰原级 right。
right 意为“右边”，no less right than 表示“其右边不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之右边不亚于任何人的预料。
right 意为“右边”，母亲 1986 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的右边右手”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1974 年，掌柜在账本里记下了一件正确的答案。（a right answer to the sum）
它正确到铺子里没有一个人敢靠近。（so right that …）
母亲觉得它太正确，谁也用不上。（too right to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩右边的右手。（a right hand of the driver）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩司机的右手一样右边。（as right as …）
到了 1981 年，账本上只剩半行字：要的是一件右边的东西。（something right）
answers: In 1974 the shopkeeper wrote of a right answer to the sum in the account.
It was so right that nobody in the shop would go near it.
My mother thought it too right to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a right hand of the driver.
He said nobody would call it as right as the hand of the driver they had once had.
By 1981 the account asked for nothing but something right.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 right 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1974 the shopkeeper wrote of a right answer to the sum in the account, and nobody forgot it.
It was the right answer to the sum that anybody there had ever seen, or so the account says.
My mother thought it too right to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a right hand of the driver, and nobody argued with him.
The buyer from the next shop called the plan quite right, and everybody laughed.
The right ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
